Correct Spectra or Line Intensities for the Spectral Response

Source: R/response.R
correct_response.Rd

Divides spectra, or the intensities of emission lines, by the relative spectral response of the instrument measured by response_calibration().

Usage

correct_response(x, response)

Arguments

x

Spectra (a numeric vector named by wavelength, or a matrix or data frame with one spectrum per row and the wavelengths as column names), or a table of lines with wavelength and intensity columns.

response

The result of response_calibration().

Value

x, corrected. For a table of lines, with the corrected intensity (and height), its standard error intensity_se, and the response used. Channels or lines without response become NA.

Details

Spectra must have the wavelength axis of the response (the same channels, in the same order): each channel is divided by its response.

A table of lines, such as returned by line_intensities(), is recognized by its wavelength and intensity columns. The intensity (and height) of each line is divided by the response at the channel of its peak (peak_wavelength, or else the channel nearest to its wavelength), and its standard error intensity_se (created if absent) combines in quadrature its relative standard error and that of the response. Correcting the line intensities rather than the spectra keeps the noise estimates of line_intensities() valid. The errors of the response of nearby lines are correlated, which plasma_uncertainty() does not account for.

Correct the intensities for the response before correct_self_absorption(), boltzmann() or cf_libs().

See also

response_calibration(), line_intensities()

Examples

planck <- function(wl, t) 1 / (wl^5 * (exp(1.4388e7 / (wl * t)) - 1))
reference <- data.frame(wavelength = seq(250, 850, by = 10))
reference$value <- planck(reference$wavelength, 3100)
reference$rsd <- 0.03
wl <- seq(260, 840, by = 0.1)
true_response <- exp(-((wl - 500) / 250)^2)
set.seed(1)
lamp <- 2e4 * true_response * planck(wl, 3100) / planck(500, 3100) + rnorm(length(wl), sd = 20)
names(lamp) <- wl
response <- response_calibration(lamp, reference)

# a spectrum with two lines of equal emission, at 300 and 650 nm
emission <- 1000 * exp(-(wl - 300)^2 / 0.01) + 1000 * exp(-(wl - 650)^2 / 0.01)
spectrum <- stats::setNames(true_response * emission + rnorm(length(wl)), wl)
lines <- line_intensities(spectrum, c(a = 300, b = 650))
lines$intensity   # unequal: the response differs
#> [1] 72.05381 95.34854
corrected <- correct_response(lines, response)
corrected[c("line", "intensity", "intensity_se", "response")]
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>   line  intensity intensity_se response
#>   <chr>     <dbl>        <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 a          135.         5.14    0.534
#> 2 b          137.         4.10    0.698

# or the whole spectrum
corrected_spectrum <- correct_response(spectrum, response)
